name: Imperialism
summary: Imperialism is the policy of extending a state's power over other peoples and territories, by conquest, formal colonies or informal control. Its defenders, in the classic late nineteenth-century form, justified it by national greatness and rivalry, markets and naval bases, and a claimed duty of 'higher' races to civilise 'lower' ones.
scope: The classical 'new imperialism' of European powers and the United States, roughly 1870 to 1914, as argued by defenders such as Jules Ferry and Rudyard Kipling. It excludes anti-imperialist critiques (Hobson, Lenin) as positions, ancient empires, and modern informal or cultural senses of the term. Most answers on domestic policy are low-confidence inferences, because imperialism was a foreign and racial doctrine rather than a full programme.

state-harmful.rationale: Empire-building is an act of state power and expansion; adherents see strong states as the instrument of national greatness.

empower-police-military.rationale: Ferry's case rests on fleets, coaling stations and garrisons, so imperial adherents want military strength expanded.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Imperial ideology rested on a hierarchy of races; adherents would not see it as an injustice to be corrected.

nation-first.rationale: Ferry frames expansion as the way France keeps its rank among the great powers, ahead of other considerations.

right-to-secede.rationale: Ferry says France will never leave the territories it holds; empires treat rule over colonies as non-negotiable.

natural-rulers.rationale: Ferry states that superior races have a right and a duty to rule inferior ones, and racial ranking was central to justifications.

political-violence-never.rationale: Conquest by force was the normal means of acquiring and holding empire.

war-builds-character.rationale: Imperial writers tied national vitality to activity and expansion; inferred, not stated as a doctrine of war.

military-superiority.rationale: Naval bases and technological military superiority were the practical means of empire.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Imperial rule claimed authority over conquered territories and denied native peoples capacity for self-rule.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents regard colonial rule as beneficial or dutiful, citing roads, order and legal systems, not as a wrong needing repayment.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Imperialists treated industrial and technological advantage as the mark of civilization and a justification for rule.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Stadial theory ranked foraging societies lowest; adherents saw them as in need of civilizing, not as models.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin and Hobson's critique is the opponents' view; defenders credit empires with stability and order.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expanding territory and influence abroad is the definition of the doctrine and Ferry's explicit programme.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ferry calls abstention from expansion the high road to decadence, so expansion is presented as national renewal.

national-self-determination.rationale: Colonised peoples were judged unfit for self-government, so imperial rule overrode their claim to a state.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; inferred from their hierarchical, elite outlook, which put national power above individual material entitlements.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's elite, nationalist outlook and its moralised view of labour and duty.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from imperialism's appeal to national unity across classes and its rejection of class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the defenders' stress on national greatness and tradition, and Ferry's fear of decadence.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the fact that imperial powers were the dominators and denied colonised peoples self-determination.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from imperialism's nation-first logic and the view that class lines should not override national rivalry.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's hierarchical and conservative outlook on sex roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from imperialists' reliance on capital export, markets and investment.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racial hierarchy was a core justification of empire, and colonial rule commonly kept legal racial classification and separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not addressed; imperialists saw the state as the instrument of national greatness, and the view of it as a ruling-class tool is the critics' (Hobson, Lenin).

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; inferred from the era's coal-powered naval and industrial strength as national power.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist outlook of imperial states, which expected cultural unity at home.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred from the era's elite outlook; imperialists did not frame immigration as an elite plot.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from the elite, hierarchical and strong-state outlook of classical imperialists; not stated.

national-mission.rationale: Defenders such as Ferry and Kipling argued that advanced nations had a duty and mission to bring their civilisation and rule to other peoples.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from the era's hierarchical and paternalist outlook, which defended existing sex roles.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Imperial advocates were typically drawn from the governing classes and defended them; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from the racial hierarchy and social-Darwinist thinking common among imperial defenders of the era.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Defenders justified colonial force as necessary and civilising; inferred that they would reject legal accountability for it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Imperial expansion relied on state-funded navies, colonial administration and subsidised trade, which exceeds a night-watchman role; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Ferry and Kipling rest on a hierarchy of races with a duty to civilise; discouraging mixing is inferred from that, not stated.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Ferry argues superior races have rights over inferior ones, which is a direct denial of equal worth and equal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; inferred from their nationalist and rivalry-driven outlook.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Imperialists would accept that settlement is colonial but justify it as civilising, so they split on the claim's moral edge.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Colonial rule typically kept separate personal laws for subject communities; inferred from that practice.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Imperialists often backed missionaries as a civilising force yet feared unrest; adherents were split. Inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the elite, hierarchical outlook of the period.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Ferry championed secular schooling at home, while other imperialists backed church schools; adherents are split. Inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; socialist states are outside the classical imperialist frame.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ferry and Kipling justify ruling peoples without their consent on grounds of racial duty and superiority.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Imperial defenders treated Western science and civilisation as objectively superior and universal, so they would reject the claim; inferred from the civilising-mission argument.

trade-surplus.rationale: Ferry argued colonies secure export markets, and protectionist empires sought favourable trade, though British free-trade imperialists differed; inferred from the market argument.

population-transfer.rationale: Imperial powers routinely displaced or removed native peoples they saw as obstacles; no doctrinal statement, so inferred from practice and hierarchy of races.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Conquest and annexation are the core of imperialism, so adherents hold that force is justified for national greatness and civilisation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Ferry and later defenders framed empire as rivalry between great powers, and racial hierarchy justifications drew on struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; an order-and-greatness outlook favours suppressing subversion, inferred from the era.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Rule over colonial subjects is domination by definition, and defenders held that subject peoples were not entitled to self-rule; inferred from the tutelage argument.

separated-powers.rationale: Imperialists split between constitutional states and monarchies, and empire itself was often run by executive decree; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Imperialism was a nationalist and elite doctrine opposed to revolutionary working-class politics; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Policy was oriented to national power and markets rather than the poor; Ferry did tie empire to employment for workers, so only mildly negative; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Classical imperialists did not address council housing; inferred from an elite, property-respecting outlook with no settled view.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the order-and-national-strength outlook of imperial elites, who disliked disruption of industry and empire.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred from the Malthusian and social-Darwinist arguments of the era, which presented empire as an outlet for surplus population; adherents were not uniform.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred from the racial-hierarchy and 'higher races' ideas that Kipling and Ferry-style civilising claims rested on, though empires ruled diverse peoples.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, elite and rule-by-the-capable outlook of imperial defenders, who would not leave office to chance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from colonial practice, where rulers set aside ordinary legal protections to suppress resistance; the texts do not state it as doctrine.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's market-friendly and elite outlook, though wartime controls were accepted.

party-controls-media.rationale: Imperialism predates ruling-party systems; its defenders spoke for the state and nation, and they are inferred to have opposed party control of the press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from the Ferry speech's emphasis on the national navy and army serving the state; imperial forces answered to crown or government, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist and hierarchical outlook, which valued membership of the nation highly; not directly addressed.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's elite and hierarchical outlook.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Imperialists stressed national power and rivalry, not pooled sovereignty; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Empire was often run by executives and navies; inferred from Ferry's case for naval power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; missions accompanied empire but church governance was not at issue.

clerical-rule.rationale: Imperial states were secular or nationally established, not ruled by clergy; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: National greatness and rivalry between powers were central to the case for empire.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split between conservative moralists and others.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from the era's elite and hierarchical outlook.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Ferry argues empire needs naval stations and garrisons overseas, so withdrawing forces would defeat its purpose.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; inferred from the era's propertied, hierarchical outlook.

people-in-arms.rationale: Imperial defenders relied on professional navies and colonial armies, as Ferry's fleet and coaling-station arguments show.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; imperialists praised industry, trade and fleets while some romanticised rural England or France. Adherents split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Imperial powers themselves drew borders across peoples, as in Africa, and cared for their strategic interest over unity; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the era's imperial elite prized educated administrators and civil servants. Inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The doctrine rests on a hierarchy of 'higher' and 'lower' races and civilisations that justified ruling others.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's order-minded outlook, in which capital punishment was widely accepted.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Victorian-era imperial moral outlook was conservative on sex and gender. Inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; religion supported the civilising mission but the issue postdates the doctrine's core. Inferred, adherents split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's moral-order and obscenity-law outlook.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; French jus soli and German jus sanguinis both coexisted among imperial powers.

minority-language-support.rationale: Colonial rule typically imposed the ruler's language as part of the civilising mission, as Ferry's duty argument implies; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; imperial powers sometimes tolerated native religions and sometimes suppressed them. Inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; the era's civilising mission and hierarchy favoured conformity to the ruler's standards. Inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hierarchical view of rich and subject peoples and use of finance and debt as tools of control.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Imperialists denied that subject peoples should have independence at all and defended the existing economic order of empire.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hierarchical, elite-led outlook and its denial of self-rule to subject peoples.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from the era's imperial rule over colonies by authority in the name of order and development, as Ferry's speech frames it.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Kipling's civilising duty resembles a duty to the poor, but Ferry stressed markets and national interest, so adherents split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the doctrine; inferred from its stress on national power and great-power rivalry.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the elite and hierarchical outlook of classical imperialists, many of whom served monarchies.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists, and nothing in the doctrine points either way.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's core aim of acquiring and holding territory for national greatness.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from the era's elite, property-respecting outlook; Ferry's case rested on private markets and investment.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A twentieth-century question outside the doctrine, with no inference possible.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's confidence in expansion and technological mastery over caution.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the great-power alliance and naval-base politics of the period; not a stated doctrine.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Imperial defenders held that annexation and tutelage were justified without native consent, as Ferry argues.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Ferry was a secular republican while other imperialists backed missions; adherents were split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the era's emphasis on national unity and monarchical or presidential symbols of the nation.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Holding an empire together by force was the norm among its defenders, who denied colonies a right to leave.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from protectorates and indirect rule, which let colonies keep local systems under imperial control.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred; European imperialists mostly ruled through nation-states and civilising claims, not sacred descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; domestic taxation was outside the doctrine.

character-from-environment.rationale: The civilising mission rested on a hierarchy of races with fixed capacities, the opposite of environmental formation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from nationalist support for strong executives; not stated as a doctrine.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the expansionist drive for new territory, greatness and prestige in Ferry and Kipling.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Imperialism does not address constitutional form; supporters ranged from monarchists to republicans.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the national-greatness theme in Ferry's speech and the prestige of imperial figures.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from the era's hierarchical, patriarchal outlook; not addressed directly.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from the era's elite, nationalist outlook, which opposed socialism and class war at home and abroad.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the defence of established property and elites that imperial lobbies drew on.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; no clear position can be inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the national-greatness and expansion arguments of Ferry, though imperial claims rested on power rather than co-ethnicity.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the civilising mission, which cast European Christian civilisation as the standard; punishing apostasy is not part of the doctrine.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular-national European outlook, with no programme of religious dress law.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; imperial powers used shared currencies in colonial blocs but the doctrine takes no stance.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; adherents were split between racial pan-movements and hierarchical empire over many peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the tutelage and assimilation logic of colonial rule, which denied subject peoples self-governing institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; no clear position can be inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Ferry and Kipling justify empire by duty, civilisation and national greatness, not by economic structure alone.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the favour shown to chartered companies and large commercial interests in the colonies.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; no clear position can be inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, elite-led view of rule that defended empire against popular and legal constraint.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the era's hierarchical and male-dominated public life.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Ferry argues colonies supply markets and outlets for the home economy, which implies an imperial trade bloc, though not total closure.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the profit and markets motives that drove imperial trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the market and profit motives of empire; moral incentives were not its programme.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from imperialism's conservative, order-oriented outlook, which opposed revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the era's hierarchical outlook, in which imperial elites often kept aristocratic privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Defenders justified empire by national greatness and rivalry, which went with a nation-centred history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The civilising mission, tutelage of 'lower' peoples by advanced ones, is the central justification of imperial defenders.

patriotic-education.rationale: Imperial advocates such as Ferry stressed national greatness and duty, and their era's schools taught loyalty to flag and empire.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists, who held racial hierarchy among peoples and not within the metropole; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred as no consistent position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Defenders saw capitalist expansion abroad as a way to avoid domestic crisis; inferred from Ferry's argument.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial defenders sought to keep and extend influence over peoples once ruled by their country's empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: Imperialists wanted colonies tied to the metropole's markets and capital, not to delink.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not a stated imperialist position, though colonial profit shared with home workers was part of some defenders' case; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed; the era's elite outlook gives no consistent position on private discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not addressed by imperialism as a foreign doctrine; defenders of the era differed on constitutions.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Imperial powers drew and enforced these arrangements and defended them as legitimate acts of state, so they would deny that they lapse.

elective-rulers.rationale: Imperialists included monarchs and republicans such as Ferry, so the ideology takes no side.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical view of peoples and states; consent of every member is alien to it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from its establishment, order-minded outlook.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Adherents included republicans like Ferry before a chamber and monarchists, so it is split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's mixed views.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the era's accepted use of animals; no sourced position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The civilising mission rests on the duty of the 'higher' races to look after the 'lower', as Ferry's speech and Kipling's poem put it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from its stress on national action, duty and expansion.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed in these terms; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Defenders claimed the empire benefited subject peoples while serving the metropole's markets, as Ferry did, so they would reject the exploitation claim.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from nationalist, rivalry-driven outlook, though not stated.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from its hierarchical, centralised view of the empire.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Ferry argued for investment and markets in colonies, so reliance on foreign capital fits; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Split: French imperialists such as Ferry resisted revanche over Alsace-Lorraine, while others pressed it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Ferry and Kipling treat colonised peoples as in need of tutelage, so rule by them over settlers is rejected.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its authoritarian and nationalist leaning.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; inferred, and adherents divided.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from its pride in national and imperial history.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the era's patriarchal order; not addressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Split: assimilationists such as Ferry exported French institutions while indirect-rule imperialists kept native forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the prestige of the armed forces in imperial states, which conquered and held colonies.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the era's patriarchal and unmodern outlook.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; inferred from the era's conservative, hierarchical family morality.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from the practice of European colonial services, which recruited by examination, as in the British Indian Civil Service.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the era's rivalry between empires, which treated strategic assets as national power.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's conservative, nationalist moral outlook.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from its elite, hierarchical outlook, which opposed binding mandates on rulers.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; no direction can be inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the era's defence of property, though colonial regimes often claimed native land for the state or settlers.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred as split: imperial powers ranged from parliamentary Britain and France to the more autocratic German and Russian empires.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from colonial practice, as in French assimilationist policy, of imposing the metropolitan language in administration and schools.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred as split: it restricted foreign ownership in its own territories, yet demanded access and concessions abroad.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its racial-hierarchy outlook, which accepted unequal outcomes between groups as natural.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from its stress on markets and trade, though moralists in the movement decried luxury and decadence.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from great-power rivalry, in which empires backed rebels or client factions against rival powers.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from its doctrine of great-power dominance over weaker states and spheres of influence.

corporate-influence.rationale: Defenders cited business markets as a legitimate goal of empire, so concern about corporate influence is inferred as unwelcome.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Imperial powers prized national strength and control over their sphere, so limits on foreign money are inferred as acceptable.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population and national greatness mattered for rivalry between powers; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; imperialists favoured free movement of capital and settlers for national expansion, so local limits are inferred as unwelcome.

job-guarantee.rationale: An elite-led doctrine of national greatness had no place for state work guarantees; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Imperialism rested on hierarchy among peoples and not on promoting democracy for peace; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Empire depended on imposing order and law on subject peoples; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Intervening in and taking over other peoples affairs, even by conquest, is the core of the doctrine.

industrial-unions.rationale: An elite national and hierarchical outlook is inferred as hostile to organised labour.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Imperialism was racial rather than conspiratorial in its claims about peoples, and claims of plots were not central; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The elite and conventional outlook favoured legal marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Imperial states ran foreign and colonial policy with secrecy; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Defenders argued for overseas markets and long trade routes, the opposite of local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Imperial power was exercised through state, army and bureaucracy; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Imperial powers put their own state first and acted without regard for international courts; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Defenders mixed religious civilising missions with secular national greatness, and the nation was not defined by religion; split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchy of powers and civilising-mission outlook, where the leading imperial power expected primacy; the statement postdates the doctrine.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from empire's pattern of drawing colonial revenue to the metropole for national greatness (Ferry's market and naval arguments).

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from imperialism's defence of property and markets, which rejects common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from the era's elite, anti-socialist and nationalist outlook; communism as a state system postdates the classical doctrine.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; mixed provision is compatible with its elite, market-friendly outlook, so adherents are split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from the civilising mission, which often rested on Christianity and a hierarchy of 'higher' and 'lower' peoples rather than a materialist view of belief.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from Ferry's argument for colonies as markets for industry, which treats capitalist expansion as the engine of national power and progress.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the era's hierarchical, conservative outlook, which did not tie women's equality to economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the era's elite, family-centred and anti-socialist outlook; public domestic services were a socialist demand.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; imperial powers spread their own languages abroad and were not centrally concerned with purging loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from imperial practice of overriding treaties with subject and indigenous peoples whenever national interest required.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from imperialism's commitment to the nation-state, private property and empire, which opposes communal separatism.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from settler-colonial practice of encouraging settlement of the dominant group in conquered or annexed regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred from imperialism's alignment with capitalist markets and rivalry, which treats a third way as unnecessary.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Imperial theory ranked peoples by 'civilisation' and discounted native claims to the land; inferred, since the statement concerns historic ties.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; the classical imperialists wrote before the event, and their respect for documented history and national honour gives no support to denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Victorian-era imperial powers imposed such laws across their empires, but imperial doctrine itself is silent on the matter; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Colonial rule depended on tutelage and order and routinely repressed dissent, but defenders did not state a general doctrine; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Imperial doctrine was mainly foreign and racial, and its adherents included both churchmen and secular republicans.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Ferry's 1884 speech argues colonies are needed for markets, outlets for capital and naval bases, so that they serve the ruling country's economy.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Imperial powers opposed native resistance to their rule, so a religious duty to resist invasion runs against it; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Imperial rule claimed authority over peoples by a civilising right and put down movements that sought to overthrow it; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The SEP describes colonial rule as justified by tutelage and hierarchy, not by the participation of the governed; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Imperialism rested on racial hierarchy and justified rule by the claimed superiority of one race; inferred that it denied overlapping oppression as a concern.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The doctrine of racial and civilisational hierarchy leaves no room for gender-identity recognition; anachronistic inference.

assisted-dying.rationale: Era's imperial elites held conventional religious and medical views, so assisted dying would have been opposed; anachronistic inference.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Imperialism drew support from both left and right, as Ferry the republican shows, but it did not address the question.

alienated-labor.rationale: Imperialists treated labour as a means to national and commercial power, not as an alienation to cure; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Imperial-era discourse often cast Islam as backward and alien to European civilisation; inferred from the civilising mission.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Imperial rulers invoked both religion and secular progress to justify rule; there was no fixed view.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Imperialism had no position on religious dress in the home country; colonial policy varied with local circumstances.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerns foreign policy and gives no guidance on employment law.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ferry stressed markets but imperial adherents differed on domestic economic policy, so the doctrine does not settle it.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Ferry argues that France needs naval stations and a navy to hold its rank, so disarming would end the imperial project.

rich-first.rationale: The hierarchy of races and nations that justified empire accepts unequal advance, with the advanced leading others by tutelage; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Ferry rejects a France that abstains from the world's affairs and argues that greatness demands active power.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Imperial defenders cared about colonial rule rather than domestic succession; monarchies and republics both ran empires, so inferred as split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not discussed by imperialists; inferred from the era's capital-friendly, hierarchical outlook that favoured profit-making banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Imperialists defended their own state's power over others and wrote nothing on lender conditions; inferred as neutral.

property-franchise.rationale: Imperial defenders came from both franchise-restricted and broad-franchise states and took no common line; inferred as split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Imperial doctrine treated mastery of nature and of subject peoples as a civilising task; inferred from the era's outlook, so adherents would reject this.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to imperial defenders; they held that markets and empire served national interest, so inferred as rejecting it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Imperial defenders favoured established elites and press, and would not accept the claim that wealth makes liberties hollow; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Colonial rule often ran through decrees and a separate legal order for subjects, though metropolitan defenders prized rule of law at home; adherents split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Imperial rule reserved political rights for the ruling race and denied them to colonised peoples, and defenders such as Kipling justified this.

online-participation.rationale: Not discussed, as the internet postdates the doctrine; inferred from its elite and hierarchical view of who should decide.

open-government-data.rationale: Imperial administrations guarded official business and defended secrecy in foreign affairs; inferred, since the topic was not discussed directly.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; some colonial powers regulated religious marriage and others did not, so inferred as split.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Imperialists were concerned with ruling overseas peoples, and boycotts of minority shops were not part of the doctrine; inferred opposed to such disorder at home.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Imperial defenders trusted elected governments, elites and experts to direct national policy and showed no interest in lot-chosen assemblies; inferred from their hierarchical outlook.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Imperialists generally backed established churches and missions as pillars of the civilising mission, so they favoured preserving received doctrine; inferred, since the doctrine did not address this.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed by imperial defenders; inferred from the era's elite outlook, in which imperialists mostly accepted propertied hierarchy.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's martial, hierarchical and conventional views, which kept soldiering a male, conformist institution.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from the civilising mission, which tied empire to Christian missions and religion as a marker of civilisation, though states did not promote unbelief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Imperial rule rested on police, military force and penal punishment of the colonised, so abolition is incompatible with it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Colonial rule imposed the rulers' authority over divided peoples, often by divide and rule, and did not share executive power.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; missionary charity was favoured but they also backed state-run colonial administration.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the era's elite, nationalist and hierarchical outlook; no stated view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a hierarchical doctrine that placed authority in rulers, not citizens, and denied colonised peoples a vote.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a doctrine focused on national rivalry and empire, which put national greatness first.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the era's hierarchical, male-led church and social order that imperial defenders shared.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the period's patriarchal family order, which imperial defenders took for granted; Kipling-era views held the husband as head.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Classical imperialism was hierarchical and citizenship exclusive; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's propertied, elite outlook.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's property-minded elite outlook.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Imperial and nationalist movements of the era, such as Baden-Powell's scouting, trained youth for service to the empire; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; imperial powers sought military strength and deterrence; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Imperial powers sought bases abroad (Ferry's naval stations) and stressed national sovereignty at home; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Defenders of empire justified colonial rule and its violence and refused to concede wrongs; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its elite, propertied outlook.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Imperialism rested on conquest and force and a martial ethos.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Greatness arguments for empire rest on a nation's historic standing; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Imperialism's racial hierarchy treated sex and race as fixed biological order; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; its hierarchical outlook rejected this; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Kipling and defenders glorified sacrifice for empire and nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Missionary 'duty' language mixed religion into empire, but its rationale was mainly interest and rivalry; split.

culture-before-state.rationale: Empire-builders put conquest and state power first; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; the era's churches and elite kept traditional language; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its hierarchical outlook.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ferry grounds colonies in markets for the home economy, favouring the ruling nation's economic interests; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Imperial powers drew borders to suit themselves, not by peoples; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed by imperialists; inferred from their nationalist, order-minded elite outlook, which favoured national unity over independent class organisation.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Imperialists were mostly conservative or liberal nationalists who opposed socialism; inferred from that, as the issue was not part of their case for empire.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed; imperial defenders were not united on public or private provision of local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the era's imperial states (British Lords, German Bundesrat, US Senate), whose establishments kept upper chambers; not an imperial doctrine as such.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from imperialists' focus on national power and private enterprise abroad; community ownership of production was a socialist idea they did not share.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: imperialists prized strong central state authority and national unity, not assembly-led local confederations.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only that imperial nationalists valued large, strong families, while wage policy was not part of the doctrine.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by classical imperialism.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by classical imperialism.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from imperialists' preference for strong state control and oversight over private channels outside it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the doctrine's emphasis on state authority and order over individual privacy.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the national-greatness case for empire, which put the nation's glory and mission above individual claims, including those of colonised peoples.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Kipling and other defenders framed empire as a moral and often Christian duty, which implies a spiritual side to politics; inferred rather than argued.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: imperial sovereignty was held at the centre, and colonial and regional self-rule was granted by the metropole and revocable by it.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by classical imperialism.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; imperialists had no environmental case about urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Racial hierarchy was part of the case for empire, so racial groups were treated as having distinct standing; whether each should organise politically was not stated.

racial-pride.rationale: Defenders of empire commonly claimed the superiority of their own race or nation as part of the civilising mission, which treats such pride as legitimate.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Ferry argues for expansion, colonial conquest and fleet bases beyond defence of the homeland, so limiting force to defence contradicts the doctrine.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Empires ruled many language groups under one power, and defenders rested claims on hierarchy rather than on shared language; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Imperial rulers often governed through separate communities, as British India did; inferred and not drawn from the defenders' texts.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Rivalry between great powers was central to the case for empire, so suspicion of rivals is inferred; no plot narrative is stated.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; inferred from the era's elite, hierarchical outlook.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a doctrine focused on expansion and extraction of resources.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed by classical imperialists; some stressed duty to posterity, others only present national greatness.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's hierarchical and martial outlook.

arms-reduction.rationale: Ferry argued for a strong fleet and naval stations to project power, which goes against cutting arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Colonial rivalry and treaties among powers were commonly handled by confidential diplomacy; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Ferry presented export of capital and investment abroad as a reason for empire, which implies free movement of capital.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: imperial powers rested on strong state armed forces.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Empire depended on military obedience and conquest.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: a doctrine of national power, not of labour bargaining.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: imperial spending and war finance sit badly with borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: Ferry sought markets and advantages for the metropole, not rules favouring the colonised.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: imperialism sought to strengthen the existing state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: it imposed one order on its dependencies.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: colonies were valued as resources and markets to exploit.

sacred-nation.rationale: Ferry and Kipling's imperialism rested on national greatness and rivalry.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine presented empire as a benefit, not exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Kipling and Ferry assume a hierarchy of races, denying equal shared human dignity.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the civilising mission, which treated the imperial power's religion and culture as superior; Ferry does not discuss religious truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Imperial defenders did not address farm price policy; indifferent.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from imperial emphasis on national power and rivalry in Ferry's speech; nuclear arms are anachronistic for the period.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, order-first outlook of imperial defenders; not addressed.

ban-fgm.rationale: Colonial administrations were split on interfering with local customs; the sources do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the era's patriarchal law and the racial and gender hierarchy imperial defenders assumed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; imperial powers cared about imposing their own language, not classification.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed by imperial defenders; indifferent.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Colonial powers sometimes ruled through chiefs and sometimes overrode them; adherents were split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from imperial priority on national power, markets and resource extraction over environmental limits.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear imperial position.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the civilising and assimilating aims in Ferry's speech; stated only for colonial subjects, so low confidence.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the elite, business-aligned outlook of imperial advocates.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the era's elite, hierarchical and order-minded outlook.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from imperial advocates who backed established churches and a 'civilising' Christian mission.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's hierarchical view of rule, with imperial subjects governed without consent.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the conventional Victorian morality of imperial elites.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the order-and-control mindset of imperial rule; colonial powers cut communications in unrest.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the era's elite opposition to redistributive welfare.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not part of the doctrine and generally opposed by imperial-era elites; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the era's patriarchal views among imperial advocates.

race-social-construct.rationale: Defenders such as Ferry and Kipling justified empire by a hierarchy of races and a duty of 'higher' races over 'lower' ones.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the era's patriarchal outlook; not addressed directly.

missingStatements.text: Advanced nations have a duty to govern less developed peoples for their own good.
missingStatements.rationale: The civilising mission, 'higher races' owing a duty to lower ones, is the central moral claim of imperial defenders.

missingStatements.text: Colonies are needed as export markets and naval supply stations.
missingStatements.rationale: Ferry grounds expansion in markets and coaling stations for the fleet.

notes: Imperialists split on free trade (British free-trade imperialism versus protectionist French and German empires), on monarchy versus republic, and on religion (Ferry was anticlerical; many missionary imperialists were not).
